downsides.mod: Player gains: Take 600 Chaos Damage per second during any Flask Effect (Searing Exarch)
downsides.why: Deals 600 chaos damage per second while any flask effect is active, utility flasks included. Deadliest for life builds that keep flasks running (flask-piano, Pathfinder-style) and have low chaos resistance or little life regeneration. Players report mystery damage over time from it and deaths while another flask was still running. Chaos Inoculation characters are immune to chaos damage, so it does nothing to them.

downsides.mod: Player gains: 30% chance to be targeted by a Meteor when you use a Flask (Searing Exarch)
downsides.why: Each flask press has a 30% chance to drop a meteor on you: a spell hit, mostly fire with some physical, that can one-shot. One player with 84% fire resistance and 4600 ES was one-shot, often with the warning marker hidden under monsters. Builds with low fire resistance, low physical mitigation, or that rely on evading spells are most at risk.

downsides.mod: Player gains: (20-40)% increased Flask Charges used / (40-60)% reduced Flask Effect Duration (Searing Exarch)
downsides.why: Cuts flask uptime. Hurts builds that need permanent utility flasks (Granite or Jade flasks, ailment-immunity suffixes, Taste of Hate-style conversion), Pathfinder or flask-based mitigation, and builds that recover through life flasks.

downsides.mod: Map boss / Eldritch Minions gain: Enemies lose 6 Flask Charges every 3 seconds and cannot gain Flask Charges for 6 seconds after being Hit (Searing Exarch)
downsides.why: Once you are hit, flask charges drain and cannot be regained, so flask uptime is lost mid-fight. Most exposed: builds using life flasks as main recovery or utility flasks for defence or ailment immunity.

downsides.mod: Player gains: (-60 to -40)% to Fire Resistance / Chaos Resistance (Searing Exarch)
downsides.why: Deadly for builds without large fire overcap and for life builds near 0% or negative chaos resistance. Maxroll says to overcap fire and chaos for Exarch. Chaos Inoculation builds ignore the chaos half.

downsides.mod: Player gains: (-60 to -40)% to Cold Resistance / Lightning Resistance (Eater of Worlds)
downsides.why: Deadly for builds without large cold or lightning overcap. Maxroll advises carrying excess resistances on Eater altars because Eater minions and bosses add cold and lightning damage and penetration.

downsides.mod: Player gains: (-60 to -40)% additional Physical Damage Reduction (Eater of Worlds)
downsides.why: Weight 1000. Sharply raises physical damage taken. Armour, Endurance Charge and Juggernaut-style builds lose most of their mitigation, and builds with none go below zero. One of the most broadly dangerous downsides because almost every monster deals physical hits.

downsides.mod: Player gains: Nearby Enemies Gain 100% of their Physical Damage as Extra Fire / Chaos / Cold / Lightning Damage (both altars)
downsides.why: Exarch rolls fire or chaos; Eater rolls cold or lightning. Every nearby monster's physical hits roughly double, with the extra in the named type. Builds weak to that element take the most; chaos is the riskiest for life builds with low chaos resistance.

downsides.mod: Player gains: -3000 to Armour / -3000 to Evasion Rating (Searing Exarch)
downsides.why: A flat loss. Players say it hurts armour builds most, since 3000 can be most of their base armour; proportionally it also costs hybrid builds with moderate armour or evasion. ES or CI builds with near-zero armour and evasion barely notice it.

downsides.mod: Player gains: All Damage taken from Hits can Scorch you / (25-35)% chance to be Scorched when Hit (Searing Exarch)
downsides.why: Scorch lowers your elemental resistances by up to 30% for 4 seconds, depending on the hit's fire damage. Dangerous on elemental-heavy maps, with elemental-heavy bosses, and for builds sitting exactly at cap; stacks badly with resistance-loss downsides. Elemental ailment immunity avoids it.

downsides.mod: Player gains: (15-20)% chance for Enemies to drop Burning Ground when Hitting you (Searing Exarch)
downsides.why: Adds fire damage-over-time ground (no more than once every 2 seconds). Worst for melee and low-mobility builds that stand in packs, and builds without strong life regeneration or fire resistance.

downsides.mod: Player gains: (25-35)% chance for Enemies to drop Chilled / Shocked Ground when Hitting you (Eater of Worlds)
downsides.why: Shocked ground makes you take 15% increased damage from all sources by default; chilled ground slows your actions by 10%. At most once every 2 seconds. Mostly threatens melee and low-mobility builds in packs; shocked ground is worse for builds that already take big hits.

downsides.mod: Player gains: Curses you inflict are reflected back to you (Searing Exarch)
downsides.why: Your own curses land on you. Dangerous for hex builds, especially with Flammability or elemental-resistance curses. One player had a Profane Proxy hex applied to them as soon as they entered the map.

downsides.mod: Player gains: (10-20)% reduced Recovery Rate of Life, Mana and Energy Shield per Endurance Charge (Eater of Worlds)
downsides.why: Weight 400. Scales with endurance charges, cutting leech, regen and flask recovery for life, mana and ES. One player with 4 endurance charges lost about 72% of mana recovery and their mana regeneration effectively stopped. Cripples regen- and leech-reliant builds that run many charges.

downsides.mod: Player gains: (30-50)% reduced Defences per Frenzy Charge (Eater of Worlds)
downsides.why: Weight 400. Frenzy-charge stackers (common on bow and attack builds) can lose most or all of their armour, evasion and ES. Builds with no frenzy charges are unaffected.

downsides.mod: Player gains: (-40 to -20)% to Critical Strike Multiplier per Power Charge (Eater of Worlds)
downsides.why: Weight 400. A pure damage loss for crit builds that keep power charges up; does not affect survival and does nothing to non-crit builds. Replaced the old cooldown-recovery-per-Power-Charge downside in 3.21.

downsides.mod: Player gains: Projectiles are fired in random directions (Eater of Worlds)
downsides.why: Weight 400. Cripples single-target damage for projectile builds (bows, wands, Ballista, projectile spells, minion projectile skills). Several forum 'bug' reports of skills spraying randomly turned out to be this altar.

downsides.mod: Player gains: All Damage taken from Hits can Sap you / (25-35)% chance to be Sapped when Hit (Eater of Worlds)
downsides.why: Sap makes you deal up to 20% less damage. A damage loss rather than a death risk; elemental ailment immunity ignores it.

downsides.mod: Map boss gains: Create Consecrated Ground on Hit, lasting 6 seconds / Eldritch Minions gain: Create Consecrated Ground on Death (Searing Exarch)
downsides.why: Enemy consecrated ground gives monsters on it 5% of max life regenerated per second and 50% reduced curse effect; it does nothing to you. Hurts low-DPS, slow damage-over-time and curse-reliant builds that may not out-damage the regen.

downsides.mod: Map boss gains: Hits always Ignite / Gain (70-130)% of Physical Damage as Extra Fire Damage / All Damage can Ignite (Searing Exarch)
downsides.why: Weight 1000 (the standalone ignite version is weight 0). The boss deals much more fire damage and every hit ignites. Dangerous without ignite immunity or avoidance and with low fire resistance or low life regeneration.

downsides.mod: Map boss gains: Gain (70-130)% of Physical Damage as Extra Chaos Damage / Poison on Hit / All Damage from Hits can Poison (Searing Exarch)
downsides.why: Dangerous for life builds with low chaos resistance and builds with no poison mitigation, since poison stacks build quickly when every hit applies one. CI is immune to chaos damage, but the physical part of a hit can still poison you.

downsides.mod: Map boss gains: Gain (50-80)% of Physical Damage as Extra Fire Damage / Cover Enemies in Ash on Hit (Searing Exarch)
downsides.why: Covered in Ash gives you 20% less movement speed and 20% increased fire damage taken, on top of the boss's added fire. Worst for builds that survive by dodging and moving and builds with low fire resistance.

downsides.mod: Map boss gains: Gain (50-80)% of Physical Damage as Extra Cold Damage / Cover Enemies in Frost on Hit (Eater of Worlds)
downsides.why: Covered in Frost gives you 50% less critical strike chance and 20% increased cold damage taken. Cuts boss DPS heavily for crit builds and adds risk for builds with low cold resistance.

downsides.mod: Map boss gains: Hits always Shock / Gain (70-130)% of Physical Damage as Extra Lightning Damage / All Damage can Shock (Eater of Worlds)
downsides.why: Weight 1000. Every boss hit shocks you, raising all damage taken, on top of a large lightning damage boost. Dangerous without shock avoidance or elemental ailment immunity and with low lightning resistance.

downsides.mod: Map boss gains: Gain (50-80)% of Physical Damage as Extra Damage of a random Element / Damage Penetrates (15-25)% of Enemy Elemental Resistances (both altars)
downsides.why: Penetration lowers your effective resistance for the damage calculation only, so builds sitting at cap take noticeably more elemental damage. Especially dangerous without extra maximum resistance.

downsides.mod: Map boss / Eldritch Minions gain: +10% to maximum Fire and Chaos Resistance, +80% to Fire and Chaos Resistance (Searing Exarch); Eater version: Cold and Lightning
downsides.why: A damage wall: builds whose damage is mostly that element lose most of their damage against affected targets. Exarch version hits fire and chaos builds (ignite, fire spells, poison or chaos DoT); Eater version hits cold and lightning builds. Rule of thumb: cold/lightning builds take Exarch (red) altars, fire/chaos builds take Eater (blue).

downsides.mod: Map boss / Eldritch Minions gain: Prevent +(20-30)% of Suppressed Spell Damage / +100% chance to Suppress Spell Damage (Eater of Worlds)
downsides.why: Weight 1000. Targets take roughly 60-70% less from your spell hits and from ailments those hits inflict (ignite, poison). A large damage wall for spell builds; attack, minion and non-ailment DoT builds are unaffected.

downsides.mod: Map boss gains: +50000 to Armour / (100-200)% increased Armour and Evasion; Eldritch Minions gain: +50000 to Armour / (250-500)% increased Evasion Rating (Searing Exarch)
downsides.why: Armour only reduces physical hits, so these mostly hurt physical hit builds (melee slams, physical bows); big evasion hurts low-accuracy attack builds. Spell, elemental, DoT and Resolute Technique builds largely ignore them.

downsides.mod: Map boss gains: (50-70)% additional Physical Damage Reduction (Eater of Worlds)
downsides.why: Sharply cuts physical hit damage against the boss. Bad for low-DPS physical attack builds; elemental, chaos and DoT builds care much less.

downsides.mod: Map boss gains: Gain (50-70)% of Maximum Life as Extra Maximum Energy Shield (Eater of Worlds)
downsides.why: The boss gets 50-70% more effective HP. A time cost for low-DPS and slow DoT builds rather than a death risk, unless your build depends on a short boss phase.

downsides.mod: Map boss gains: Nearby Enemies are Hindered, with 40% reduced Movement Speed (Searing Exarch)
downsides.why: Slows you by 40% near the boss. Most dangerous for builds that dodge boss mechanics or slams by moving or kiting, such as ranged glass cannons and mobile melee. Tanky face-tank builds are less affected.

downsides.mod: Map boss gains: 100% Global chance to Blind Enemies on hit / (100-200)% increased Blind Effect (Eater of Worlds)
downsides.why: Blind lowers accuracy and evasion rating by 20%, more with the increased effect. Mainly hurts attack builds relying on accuracy and evasion. Resolute Technique and spell builds are largely unaffected.

downsides.mod: Eldritch Minions gain: Gain (70-130)% of Physical Damage as Extra Damage of a random Element / Inflict Fire, Cold, and Lightning Exposure on Hit (Searing Exarch)
downsides.why: Exposure usually lowers the matching resistance by 25%, and these minions apply all three. Builds without overcap or with low maximum resistance can drop well below cap during pack fights.

downsides.mod: Eldritch Minions gain: 100% chance to remove a random Charge from Enemy on Hit (Eater of Worlds)
downsides.why: Weight 1000. Each minion hit strips one of your Power, Frenzy or Endurance charges, so charge-reliant builds lose those bonuses in pack fights. In 3.29.3 GGG fixed Zana's Ingenuity's 'cannot steal or remove charges' mod, which had not worked against certain altar mods.

downsides.mod: Eldritch Minions gain: Skills fire (3-5) additional Projectiles (Eater of Worlds)
downsides.why: Weight 1000. Extra projectiles can shotgun, so big eldritch packs hit much harder. Dangerous for low-EHP builds, especially without block, evasion, spell suppression or projectile avoidance.

downsides.mod: Eldritch Minions gain: Hits have (50-80)% chance to ignore Enemy Physical Damage Reduction (Eater of Worlds)
downsides.why: Influenced monsters bypass your armour and physical damage reduction most of the time. Dangerous for armour and Endurance Charge builds that rely on physical mitigation.

downsides.mod: Eldritch Minions gain: Inflict 1 Grasping Vines on Hit (Eater of Worlds)
downsides.why: Each stack gives 8% less movement speed, capped at 10 stacks (80%) for most sources. Instant-teleport movement skills such as Flame Dash remove all stacks; slow builds without one can get pinned in packs.

downsides.mod: Eldritch Minions gain: (70-130)% increased Area of Effect (Searing Exarch)
downsides.why: Enlarges monster AoE skills. One player reported oversized explosions but still took it, reasoning some monster skills would one-shot him anyway.

downsides.mod: Eldritch Minions gain: Drops Burning Ground (Exarch) / Chilled or Shocked Ground (Eater) on Death
downsides.why: Ground effects left on death mostly threaten melee builds that fight in packs and corpses; ranged builds can usually ignore them. Since 3.18 the burning ground no longer scales off the monster's main-hand attack damage.

upsides.mod: Map boss gains: Final Boss drops (2-4) additional Divine Orbs (Eater of Worlds)
upsides.note: Top-value upside and Eater-only (Exarch version is weight 0). Weight 1000, about 0.1% of Eater boss-upside rolls, against 160000 for Alteration or Jeweller's. Always take it when the boss is still alive.

upsides.mod: Eldritch Minions gain: (1.6-3.2)% chance to drop an additional Divine Orb (Eater of Worlds)
upsides.note: Minion version of the Divine altar, weight 1000, very rare. Payout depends on how many influenced monsters you kill.

upsides.mod: Map boss gains: Final Boss drops (2-4) additional [Breach / Delirium / Legion / Blight / Ritual / Harvest / Ultimatum / Abyss / Expedition / Betrayal / Bestiary / Incursion / Sulphite / Kalguuran] Scarabs (Eater of Worlds)
upsides.note: Weight 3187 each, about 4% of Eater boss-upside rolls combined. Value depends on which scarab type is currently expensive; a boss scarab altar for an in-demand mechanic is worth clicking. Minion version: (1.6-3.2)% chance per eldritch minion.

upsides.mod: Map boss gains: Final Boss drops (2-4) additional [Influence / Cartography / Divination / Anarchy / Miscellaneous / Beyond / Torment / Ambush / Domination / Essence / Titanic / Trarthan] Scarabs (Searing Exarch)
upsides.note: Weight 1584 each, about half the per-type weight of Eater scarabs (about 4.5% of Exarch boss-upside weight combined). Trarthan = Mercenaries scarabs, added in 3.29.

upsides.mod: Player gains: Scarabs / Basic Currency / Unique Items dropped by slain Enemies have (15-30)% chance to be Duplicated (both altars)
upsides.note: Applies map-wide to everything killed for the rest of the map. Scarab duplication is most valuable on scarab-heavy atlas strategies. Taking it means accepting a player-targeted downside.

upsides.mod: Player gains: Maps / Divination Cards dropped by slain Enemies have (15-30)% chance to be Duplicated (both altars)
upsides.note: Players report the divination card and map duplicate upsides rarely produce anything; one called them a free downside. Only worth it on card-heavy strategies.

upsides.mod: Player gains: (10-20)% increased Quantity of Items found in this Area / (15-30)% increased Rarity of Items found in this Area (both altars)
upsides.note: Two separate mods since 3.26; the most common player upsides. Quantity boosts only normal drops, not eldritch-exclusive rewards; works best with quantity-focused, blue-altar strategies. Stacks across altars.

upsides.mod: Map boss / Eldritch Minions gain: Exarch currency (Binding, Unmaking, Scouring, Annulment, Vaal, Enkindling, Instilling, Regret, Glassblower's Bauble, Gemcutter's Prism, Chaos Orb, Lesser/Greater/Grand Eldritch Embers)
upsides.note: Maxroll: frequent low- and mid-tier currency, a reliable income source especially at league start. Annulment is rare (weight 1000); Chaos Orb weight 48000. Scouring moved here from Eater in 3.28. Also rolls on minions.

upsides.mod: Map boss / Eldritch Minions gain: Chromatic / Fusing / Alteration / Jeweller's Orbs (Eater of Worlds)
upsides.note: Low-value basic currency; players skip altars when both rewards are like minion Chromatics against boss Fusings. Also rolls on the boss.

upsides.mod: Map boss / Eldritch Minions gain: Divination Cards rewarding Unique Weapon/Armour/Jewellery, Corrupted Unique, Map, Unique Map or Corrupted Item (Searing Exarch)
upsides.note: Exarch-only card pool since 3.20; Unique Map cards are rare (weight 2264). Boss-exclusive cards cannot come from altars since 3.25.

upsides.mod: Map boss / Eldritch Minions gain: Divination Cards rewarding Basic Currency, League Currency, other Cards, Gems, Levelled or Quality Gems (Eater of Worlds)
upsides.note: Eater-only card pool since 3.20; Basic Currency cards are the most common (weight 230076).

rules.text: Every altar option targets one of three things: Player gains (Maxroll calls these 'Global'), Map Boss gains, or Eldritch Minions gain. Each pairs one downside with one upside.

Skip player/global altars unless you are experienced. Player downsides follow you everywhere in the map; boss and minion downsides only affect those monsters. Maxroll says the Searing Exarch global mods are barely runnable for most builds and recommends globals mainly on Eater altars for magic-find, Harvest or Expedition farming.
Clear every eldritch monster around an altar before reading it: the game does not pause while you read. Check taken mods by hovering the altar icon in the lower right.

Minion rewards are ranked strongest and safest by Maxroll; GGG tuned boss rewards to be slightly better on average and combines boss currency into one stack. Take boss rewards when the boss is easy for your build or offers more valuable currency; take minion rewards when many influenced packs remain.
Boss upsides drop a fixed (2-4) extra items; minion upsides give each eldritch minion a (1.6-3.2)% chance at one item, so minion payout scales with influenced kills.

Boss options cannot appear once the map boss is dead or before it spawns. Kill the boss first, or run maps whose boss is not present on load (Arachnid Nest, Mausoleum, Jungle Valley), to force minion or player options.

Upsides (quantity, rarity, drop chance, duplicate chance) stack across altars; the same downside cannot appear twice. Altar effects last for the rest of the map and cannot be removed. Once boss mods are gone a map holds at most 10 Exarch or 12 Eater altars (6 with Eldritch Gaze).
Element rule of thumb: cold or lightning builds take Exarch (red) altars, fire or chaos builds take Eater (blue) altars, to avoid resistance-wall downsides on your damage type.

Wrath of the Cosmos: Exarch altars get a 50% chance of a second upside, but those altars have 100% increased downside effect (e.g. -80 to -120% resistance, 1200 chaos per second during flasks). Eldritch Gaze: Eater altars get an extra downside and 50% increased upside effect; check both downsides against your build.
Ignore altars when both rewards are low-value basic currency.

Value profiles: Exarch altars give frequent low- and mid-tier currency plus unique and corrupted card rewards (reliable, good at league start). Eater altars are a rare shot at very high-value currency such as Divines and suit later-game and quantity strategies.

Since 3.20, each specific currency, scarab and divination card reward is exclusive to one altar type, and scarabs are offered much less often. Since 3.20, influenced maps spawn 20 to 60 packs instead of a fixed 60, with more altars to compensate.

Mods with spawn weight 0 should not be expected: Eldritch Tentacles, 'Your hits inflict Malediction', standalone 'Hits always Ignite' and 'Poison on Hit', minion 'Curse Enemies with Punishment / Vulnerability on Hit', player 'Spell Hits have chance to Hinder you', the grasping-vines-while-stationary player mod, and Chaos or Divine rewards on the opposite altar.
In 3.29 any party member can click Eldritch altars. Agree who picks, because a downside can apply to everyone.

Stack pack size when farming altars, e.g. Influencing Scarab of Hordes (+40% pack size for influence monsters). Rampant Growth (Ichor duplication) and Word of the Exarch (Ember duplication) are mandatory atlas nodes; The Shadow of Hunger and The Light of Dawn significantly raise altar spawns.

mods.name: Ruin (I-IV)
mods.why: The encounter fails at 7 Ruin, and Ruin carries over between rounds. I: one monster type applies Ruin. II: double Ruin. III: two monster types apply double Ruin. IV: two types apply quadruple Ruin, close to a 2-hit fail. Tiers I-II are safe for mobile builds (about 4-7% failure in GGG's 2021 stats). Riskier before a possible Trialmaster round: if you took Ruin mods, every Trialmaster attack inflicts Ruin.

mods.name: Stalking Ruin (I-IV)
mods.why: An invulnerable shade follows you and inflicts Ruin (fail at 7). I is melee only; II-III add speed and spells. IV casts Ruin spells aggressively while teleporting, so outrunning it no longer works. Tiers I-II were among the least dangerous in GGG's 2021 stats (about 4-9% failure), but Maxroll's 3.29 strategy lists it as a modifier to avoid.

mods.name: Razor Dance (I-IV)
mods.why: Blades fly at you and apply Corrupted Blood; higher tiers add blades and IV leaves Blood ground. Among the least-failed modifiers in GGG's 2021 stats (about 3.8-6.9%), and Bleed or Corrupted Blood immunity makes it trivial. Maxroll's 3.29 strategy still lists it (as 'Sawblades') among modifiers to avoid.

mods.name: Choking Miasma (I-IV)
mods.why: A Chaos damage-over-time cloud follows you, growing faster and larger by tier; IV also slows. Mobile builds outrun it; stationary or channelling builds and low chaos resistance are punished. Tiers I-II were among the least dangerous in GGG's 2021 stats (about 4.8-7.6% failure).

mods.name: Stormcaller Runes (I-IV)
mods.why: Runes call Lightning storms if you stay in them (at IV after only a short time). Tier III was one of the highest-failure picks in GGG's 2021 stats (about 20% at area level 78+), with very high damage and possible stuns. Run-ending for channelling or turret builds, and Maxroll warns Stand Your Ground's shrinking arena makes them almost impossible to dodge in late rounds.

mods.name: Raging Dead (I-IV)
mods.why: Skulls spit Fire waves when you are near them. From III they chase you; IV fires a larger, faster wave. In 2021, tier III failed about twice as often as I-II (about 14% vs 6-7% at 78+).

mods.name: Blistering Cold (I-IV)
mods.why: Frozen pustules explode when you get close. III adds Chill and IV freezes on hit, which is dangerous for builds without Freeze immunity or avoidance.

mods.name: Quicksand (I-IV)
mods.why: Slowing pits appear and grow in size and number by tier. IV also reduces Life Recovery Rate by 50%, which hurts life-regen and leech builds and builds without slow immunity or avoidance.

mods.name: Blood Altar (I-II)
mods.why: A ring of Blood around the altar deals heavy Physical damage over time; II makes it larger. Worst in Protect the Altar, where you fight near the altar. Maxroll's 3.29 strategy lists it as a modifier to avoid.

mods.name: Limited Arena
mods.why: Makes the encounter area much smaller, leaving less room to dodge ground effects such as Runes, Miasma and Quicksand. A mid-risk pick in 2021 (about 9-10% failure).

mods.name: Reduced Recovery (I-II)
mods.why: Cuts Life, Mana and Energy Shield recovery rate by 60% (I) or 90% (II). Tier II can end runs for leech, regen, recoup and flask-sustain builds and for mana-hungry builds. Maxroll's 3.29 strategy lists it as a modifier to avoid.

mods.name: Less Cooldown Recovery
mods.why: Cooldowns take five times longer to recharge. Cripples builds that rely on cooldown skills (Vaal skills, guard skills, triggered or cooldown-based damage, movement skills like Flame Dash). Maxroll's 3.29 strategy lists it as a modifier to avoid.

mods.name: Treacherous Auras
mods.why: Your auras that affect allies also affect enemies, so aurabots and builds running many offensive or defensive auras hand those buffs to monsters. Maxroll's 3.29 strategy lists it as a modifier to avoid.

mods.name: Drought
mods.why: You cannot gain Flask Charges. Run-ending over a 10-round encounter for flask-reliant builds (life flasks, Bleed or Freeze immunity flasks, flask-based damage). poedb shows it with the old Limited Flasks icon; Limited Flasks was the most-failed modifier in 2021 (23.37% at 78+). Maxroll's 3.29 strategy lists it as a modifier to avoid.

mods.name: Escalating Damage Taken
mods.why: Damage taken rises 2% per second for the rest of the encounter, up to 50%. One of the two most dangerous modifiers in GGG's 2021 stats (about 19-22% failure), especially once capped. Worst for slow-clearing builds and long win conditions such as Survive.

mods.name: Occasional Impotence
mods.why: You and your minions deal no damage for 2 of every 8 seconds. One of the most-failed modifiers in 2021 (about 17-19%). Worst in Defeat waves and Protect the Altar, which depend on kill speed.

mods.name: Siphoned Charges
mods.why: You lose a Power, Frenzy and Endurance Charge every second, and monsters gain charges when they hit you. Run-ending for charge-stacking builds, harmless for builds that use no charges. About 14-17% failure in 2021.

mods.name: Lessened Reach
mods.why: Players have 60% less Area of Effect and Projectile Speed. Hits AoE-clear and projectile builds hardest. About 15-16% failure in 2021.

mods.name: Buffs Expire Faster
mods.why: Buffs on players expire five times faster. Hurts builds that rely on timed buffs such as flasks, Blood Rage or Arcane Surge.

mods.name: Hindering Flasks
mods.why: Each flask use Hinders you by 50% for 4 seconds. Dangerous for flask-pianoing builds that depend on movement. Failure was about 9% at 78+ in 2021.

mods.name: Lightning Damage from Mana Costs
mods.why: You take 1000% of your mana costs as Lightning damage. Run-ending for high-mana-cost spammers (self-cast spells and attacks paid with mana) with low lightning mitigation; harmless for life-cost or reservation-only builds.

mods.name: Random Projectiles
mods.why: Your projectiles fly in random directions and monsters fire extra projectiles. Run-ending for projectile and bow builds, fine for melee or minion builds.

mods.name: Impurity
mods.why: Players get -9% to all maximum resistances. Builds without extra maximum resistances or high life/ES pools take noticeably more elemental damage.

mods.name: Waning Spirit
mods.why: Non-curse auras from skills have 50% reduced effect on players. A major defensive and offensive loss for aura-stacking builds.

mods.name: Ailment and Curse Reflection
mods.why: Curses and non-damaging ailments you apply are reflected back on you, and monsters are unaffected by curses. Bad for hexer and curse-on-hit builds and for Freeze, Shock or Chill appliers. About 13-17% failure in 2021.

mods.name: Unlucky Criticals
mods.why: Your critical strike chance becomes Unlucky and monsters take 50% reduced extra damage from crits. A large damage loss for crit builds, safe for non-crit DoT or minion builds.

mods.name: Escalating Monster Speed
mods.why: Monsters gain 5% attack, cast and movement speed per second alive, up to 50%. Builds that kill slowly or leave monsters alive (Survive, kiting) take the full penalty.

mods.name: Precise Monsters
mods.why: Monster hits cannot be Evaded. Removes the main layer of evasion builds; treat it as run-ending for evasion builds without other mitigation.

mods.name: Overwhelming Monsters
mods.why: Monster hits Overwhelm all Physical Damage Reduction, so armour and endurance-charge tanks lose their physical mitigation.

mods.name: Deadly Monsters
mods.why: Every monster hit is a critical strike. Dangerous for builds without crit-damage reduction and on low life or low ES pools.

mods.name: Siphoning Monsters
mods.why: Each monster hit removes 10% of current Energy Shield and Mana. Dangerous for ES-based and Mind over Matter builds.

mods.name: Putrid Monsters
mods.why: Monsters Poison and Bleed on hit. Dangerous for builds without bleed or poison immunity or recovery.

mods.name: Profane Monsters
mods.why: Monsters add 80% of Physical damage as Chaos damage. Punishes weak chaos resistance.

mods.name: Prismatic Monsters
mods.why: Monsters gain 50% of Physical damage as extra damage of each element. Punishes weak elemental mitigation.

mods.name: Resistant Monsters
mods.why: Monsters have +50% to all resistances. A big damage loss for elemental-hit builds, harmless for physical or chaos builds.

mods.name: Impenetrable Monsters
mods.why: Monsters' elemental resistances cannot be penetrated. A big damage loss for elemental builds that rely on penetration, harmless for physical or chaos builds.

mods.name: Dexterous Monsters
mods.why: Monsters suppress spell damage and gain 500% increased evasion. Lowers kill speed, which matters in Defeat waves and Protect the Altar.

mods.name: Shielding Monsters
mods.why: Monsters have a 50% chance to block attack and spell damage. Lowers kill speed, which matters in Defeat waves and Protect the Altar.

mods.name: Unstoppable Monsters
mods.why: Monsters cannot be slowed or stunned. Hurts stun-lock builds and slow or Temporal Chains control builds.

mods.name: Shattered Shield
mods.why: Added in 3.28: 'You cannot Block'. The run-ending pick for block-capped builds (Gladiator, block-based aurastackers), harmless for builds that don't block.

winConditions.name: Protect the Altar
winConditions.note: Highest completion rate in GGG's 2021 stats (about 82-87% at 78+), because many monsters target the altar instead of you; strong builds finish it extremely quickly. Fails if the altar dies before enough kills. The Protect The Altar notable gives the altar +50% life. Blood Altar is worst here.

winConditions.name: Defeat waves of Enemies
winConditions.note: Completed about 82-85% of the time at 78+ in 2021; suits fast killers. Maxroll says to always take Slaughter Them All (+100% chance for this type, 20% fewer kills needed). Occasional Impotence, Dexterous and Shielding Monsters hurt here because they slow kills.

winConditions.name: Survive
winConditions.note: Little combat challenge but slow: you can kite in circles for the duration. About 81-83% completion in 2021. Survive The Assault cuts its duration by 20%. Avoid pairing it with Escalating Damage Taken or Escalating Monster Speed.

winConditions.name: Stand in the Stone Circles
winConditions.note: The hardest objective: lowest completion rate in 2021 (about 76-77%). Standing still under ground effects is what kills you. Progress is kept if you step out and come back. Maxroll calls it the worst encounter and says to avoid the Conquer The Stones notable.

rules.text: Previously chosen modifiers are more likely to come back at higher tiers, so they stack up by round 10. Skip any modifier that directly counters your build, and walk away if all three options do.
Maxroll's 3.29 strategy: walk away with the rewards you already have rather than force risky rounds, and be selective with player-affecting Eldritch Altars when combining them with Ultimatum.

Ruin carries over between rounds and every Ruin modifier fails the encounter at 7 Ruin. Your chosen modifiers still apply in the Trialmaster fight, where his attacks also inflict Ruin if you took Ruin modifiers, so stacking several Ruin mods before a possible boss round is risky.
The Trialmaster can replace round 10 (chance-based in area level 81+). All chosen modifiers apply in his fight; in 2021 he had only about 60% completion at 78+.

Failure and completion percentages quoted here are GGG's 2021 (3.14) statistics. In 3.23 Ultimatum became core: 10 rounds by default, modifiers rebalanced, and three-tier modifiers such as Stormcaller Runes got a fourth tier.

Atlas notables that raise modifier risk: Prove Yourself Worthy starts modifiers a tier higher; Stand Your Ground shrinks the radius 3% per round (rewards as if one extra round was completed), making late rounds very hard, especially with Stormcaller Runes; Gruelling Gauntlet adds 3 rounds, removes your choice of modifier and has no final boss, which can make encounters much harder or impossible.

Ruinous Wager keystone: Ultimatum monsters apply Ruin with their special abilities (fail at 7), but monsters and modifiers deal 50% less damage (the Minor Idol version: 50-60% less). Maxroll says it suits fast, squishy dodging builds.

3.29: Ultimatum is the only source of Catalysts. They were removed from Heist Demolition rewards (now Map rewards), Expedition chests, Tujen's shop and Ritual reward favours. Catalyst stack size doubled from 10 to 20.
3.29: Brave The Tower makes the Ultimatum boss drop 10 of one random Catalyst (before 3.29 it dropped a full stack, which was 10 at the time).

Sinistral and Dextral Catalysts came from Ultimatums inside Mirages in 3.28; Mirage did not become core in 3.29, so they cannot be farmed (legacy copies remain in Standard). Vendoring 3 identical Catalysts gives 1 random regular Catalyst, never Tainted, Sinistral or Dextral.

Scarabs: Catalysing makes encounters offer only Catalysts, to the map owner (limit 1). Inscription turns those Catalyst rewards into Inscribed Ultimatums (limit 1). Bribing counts rewards as 2 extra rounds and adds 150% XP (limit 2). Dueling leads to a unique boss if possible.

Maxroll's 3.29 currency setup: 2x Scarab of Bribing plus Domination, with Dueling and Inscription optional, on T16 Jungle Valley with Eldritch altars. Its avoid list: Stalking Ruin, Sawblades (Razor Dance), Reduced Recovery, Blood Altar, Less Cooldown Recovery, Treacherous Auras, Drought.

Inscribed Ultimatum: one long round with modifiers fixed at drop and a sacrificed entry item; failing loses the item (about 20% failed in 2021). You cannot reroll its modifiers, so check them against your build before running it, or sell it. Vendor 5 for 1 new one.
Maxroll's 3.29 strategy: keep Inscribed Ultimatums with 'more Monster Life' (30/70/120/200%); five matching ones trade toward rewards up to a Mirror at 200%. Vendor the rest 5:1 below roughly 20c.
3.28 added Inscribed Ultimatums that reward Ancient Orbs and Fracturing Orbs; Exalted Orb versions now give larger stacks and are easier on average.
Chaotic Astrolabe: adds a Shaped Region of Ultimatum maps. A map counts as completed only after at least 7 Ultimatum waves, and difficulty and reward rise with each completed map in the region.
Ultimatum monsters stopped dropping loot in 3.23; 3.25 restored their drops. Kirac's 'Area contains an Ultimatum Encounter' map mod costs 4 Chaos Orbs since 3.26 (was 5).

afflictions.name: Veiled Sight
afflictions.why: Every room on the Sanctum Map is hidden, so you cannot route around bad rooms or toward rewards. PoE-Vault rates it run-ending and probably the deadliest affliction, since it combines all the Smoke minors. Maxroll lists it to avoid. Always skip the Pact it comes with.

afflictions.name: Ghastly Scythe
afflictions.why: Losing any Resolve ends the Sanctum. It expires after 1, 2 or 3 rooms depending on the variant. It is a freebie with a solid Inspiration buffer, because Inspiration loss is not Resolve loss. It becomes run-ending with Spiked Exit, which takes Resolve directly and bypasses Inspiration. Take it only with Inspiration banked and without Spiked Exit.

afflictions.name: Glass Shard
afflictions.why: The next boon you gain becomes a random minor affliction, which could be a run-ender such as Deceptive Mirror or a Smoke. Run-ending early. It is a freebie late in the run, when you don't plan to collect more boons, and a cheap way to get the Pact's Offer.

afflictions.name: Unassuming Brick
afflictions.why: You cannot gain any more boons. Dangerous early, but a freebie late or when strong relics carry the run. The main reason to take it is Offer access on Floor 3 or 4.

afflictions.name: Deadly Snare
afflictions.why: Traps impact infinite Resolve, so one trap hit ends the run. PoE-Vault rates it run-ending. Maxroll says to avoid it but notes it isn't strictly run-ending. Builds with slow or rooted movement suffer most. The Imperial Seal boon disables traps.

afflictions.name: Chiselled Stone
afflictions.why: Monsters petrify you on hit. Chain-petrification can lock you down and end a run, especially in boss fights. Builds that take many hits, such as melee and face-tank builds, are most exposed.

afflictions.name: Cutpurse
afflictions.why: You cannot gain Aureus, which kills Merchant, Fountain and Offer purchases. Run-ending early. It is a freebie late only if you have already banked enough coins for the remaining Offers, Fountains and Merchants. Maxroll lists it first among majors to avoid.

afflictions.name: Orb of Negation
afflictions.why: Non-unique relics have no effect, which strips the relic Inspiration (possibly 1k+) and Merchant bonuses an Inspiration build relies on. Run-ending early. Take it only on Floor 4 with plenty of Inspiration left.

afflictions.name: Anomaly Attractor
afflictions.why: Every room spawns Volatile Anomalies. Rated dangerous because there are so many that you will get hit by some. Slow and melee builds suffer more. Take it only if needed.

afflictions.name: Death Toll
afflictions.why: You lose 250 Resolve after completing a set number of rooms (variants run from 1 to 8). The loss goes through Inspiration first, so it is manageable, and a freebie when fewer than 8 rooms remain. Patch 3.20.1b replaced its old effect (monsters drop no Aureus) with the Resolve loss.

afflictions.name: Demonic Skull
afflictions.why: You cannot recover Resolve. It is a freebie under the Inspiration strategy, because recovery barely matters when Inspiration soaks the damage. Only no-Inspiration, recovery-based setups suffer.

afflictions.name: Deceptive Mirror
afflictions.why: You are not always taken to the room you select, so it can route you into run-ending afflictions and away from Offers. PoE-Vault calls it by far the worst minor and run-ending, and Maxroll lists it to avoid. Skip it even if that means taking a worse room.

afflictions.name: Fiendish Wings
afflictions.why: Monsters get 30% increased Attack, Cast and Movement Speed and can't be slowed below base speed, which disables Chill and Temporal Chains. Rated run-ending because dodging gets much harder. Builds that rely on slows suffer most.

afflictions.name: Accursed Prism
afflictions.why: Whenever you gain an affliction, you also gain a random minor affliction. Rated run-ending because it compounds and can chain into Deceptive Mirror or a Smoke. Maxroll lists it to avoid.

afflictions.name: Purple Smoke
afflictions.why: Afflictions are hidden on the Sanctum Map, so you can walk blindly into run-ending ones. Rated run-ending. Skip.

afflictions.name: Golden Smoke
afflictions.why: Rewards are hidden on the Sanctum Map, so you can't route toward Divine Orb rewards on Floors 3 and 4. PoE-Vault rates it run-ending for profit, and Maxroll lists it to avoid.

afflictions.name: Black Smoke
afflictions.why: You see one fewer room ahead, which gives less warning of deadly rooms and means missed reward rooms, including Divines. Rated dangerous. Avoid it if possible.

afflictions.name: Red Smoke
afflictions.why: Room types are hidden. Rated a freebie because room type rarely drives decisions. The main cost is a few coins from Miniboss rooms.

afflictions.name: Floor Tax
afflictions.why: You lose all Aureus when you complete a floor. Run-ending unless you find a Merchant to spend at first. It is a freebie on Floor 4. Skip it on Floors 1 to 3.

afflictions.name: Door Tax
afflictions.why: You lose 30 Aureus per room completed, which starves Merchants, Fountains and Offers. Run-ending early, manageable late. Keep about 5 coins per remaining room so you can still afford Offers.

afflictions.name: Empty Trove
afflictions.why: Chests stop dropping Aureus, which cuts off the main coin source. Run-ending early, manageable or a freebie late or with banked coins.

afflictions.name: Worn Sandals
afflictions.why: 40% reduced Movement Speed. Rated dangerous. Manageable for very high movement-speed characters, while slow builds suffer most.

afflictions.name: Rusted Coin
afflictions.why: The Merchant offers only one choice, which overrides relics that add Merchant options. Dangerous early and a freebie late. Worst for merchant-relic setups.

afflictions.name: Poisoned Water
afflictions.why: Using a Fountain grants a random minor affliction, which effectively disables Fountains. Dangerous, but a freebie late if you just stop using Fountains.

afflictions.name: Unhallowed Ring
afflictions.why: Merchant prices go up 50%, which also devalues the coins you already hold. Dangerous early, a freebie late.

afflictions.name: Spilt Purse
afflictions.why: You lose 20 Aureus whenever a hit takes Resolve, and Inspiration loss counts too. Rated dangerous. Keep a coin buffer and spend coins before risky fights. Builds that get hit often suffer most.

afflictions.name: Rapid Quicksand
afflictions.why: Traps are faster, so boulder traps are hard to dodge without a blocking skill. Rated dangerous, and manageable only with a skill that can block them. A forum poster called Floor 4 'unplayable' with it. Avoid it, especially on Floor 4. The Imperial Seal boon disables traps.

afflictions.name: Tight Choker
afflictions.why: You can hold at most 5 boons. Rated dangerous because stacking boons matters, but manageable when strong relics reduce your reliance on boons.

afflictions.name: Unholy Urn
afflictions.why: 50% reduced effect of non-unique relics. Dangerous early, when relics provide most of your Inspiration, and a freebie late. Avoid it on Floor 1.

afflictions.name: Charred Coin
afflictions.why: 50% less Aureus found. Dangerous if taken very early on Floor 1, manageable afterwards.

afflictions.name: Dark Pit
afflictions.why: Traps impact much more Resolve: 100% increased per PoE-Vault, while PoEDB lists a 200% variant. Manageable if you move more carefully through trap rooms. Take it if needed.

afflictions.name: Spiked Exit
afflictions.why: You lose 5% of current Resolve on each room completion. It bypasses Inspiration but can't kill you on its own. A freebie with Inspiration, but run-ending without it or alongside Ghastly Scythe, and it makes Voodoo Doll dangerous. The PoE Wiki advises avoiding it early in a run.

afflictions.name: Voodoo Doll
afflictions.why: Resolve losses are doubled (100% more) while you are below 50% Resolve. Usually a freebie, because taking Pacts keeps maximum Resolve low enough that you stay above the threshold. Dangerous alongside Spiked Exit.

afflictions.name: Hungry Fangs
afflictions.why: Monsters impact 25% more Resolve, which also increases Inspiration loss. Manageable with a proper Inspiration bank; the real answer is not getting hit. Builds that tank hits feel it most.

afflictions.name: Weakened Flesh
afflictions.why: -100 Maximum Resolve (can't go below 1). A freebie under the Inspiration strategy.

afflictions.name: Haemorrhage
afflictions.why: You can't recover Resolve until the next Floor Boss dies. A freebie under the Inspiration strategy, since recovery isn't needed.

afflictions.name: Unquenched Thirst
afflictions.why: 50% reduced Resolve recovered. A freebie for the same reason as Haemorrhage: Inspiration play doesn't rely on recovery.

afflictions.name: Unhallowed Amulet
afflictions.why: The Merchant offers 50% fewer choices. Manageable, and a freebie late. Much milder than Rusted Coin because relic bonus choices still apply.

afflictions.name: Gargoyle Totem
afflictions.why: Guards come with a Gargoyle that leap-slams. Manageable with mobility and damage.

afflictions.name: Mark of Terror
afflictions.why: Monster hits inflict Resolve Weakness, which only matters after back-to-back hits. Rated manageable or a freebie.

afflictions.name: Chains of Binding
afflictions.why: Monster hits apply Binding Chains, a 20% movement slow. Manageable, because a movement skill cancels it.

afflictions.name: Rusted Mallet
afflictions.why: Monsters always knock you back, with increased distance. A freebie if you are not getting hit. PoEDB notes that patch notes removed it, though it is still listed.

afflictions.name: Concealed Anomaly
afflictions.why: Guards release a Volatile Anomaly on death. A freebie; normal movement habits avoid it.

afflictions.name: Tattered Blindfold
afflictions.why: 90% reduced Light Radius and a hidden minimap. A freebie, because room layouts are few and easy to memorise. A forum player also lists it among the least harmful minors.

afflictions.name: Spiked Shell
afflictions.why: Monsters have more maximum Life: 30% increased per PoE-Vault's pre-3.22 text, 50% more per PoEDB. A freebie for a well-built endgame character; weak single-target builds feel it. A forum player suggests the Sanguine Vial or Ornate Dagger boons as counters.

afflictions.name: Blunt Sword
afflictions.why: You and your Minions deal less damage. PoE-Vault's pre-release text says 25%, but PoEDB and a live 3.22 forum post say 40%, which is likely the live value. A freebie for endgame damage; low-DPS and minion builds struggle.

afflictions.name: Honed Claws
afflictions.why: Monsters deal more regular damage (not Resolve damage): 25% per PoE-Vault, 50% per PoEDB. Usually a freebie, but dangerous for glass-cannon builds and during the Herald's intermission phase.

boons.name: All-Seeing Eye
boons.note: Major boon that fully reveals the Sanctum Map. Maxroll lists it among the best major boons, and a forum player calls it top priority because map information is what lets you dodge bad afflictions.

boons.name: Scrying Crystal
boons.note: Lets you see one more room ahead. A forum player rates it top priority alongside All-Seeing Eye, for the same map-information reason.

boons.name: Crystal Shard
boons.note: Major boon: your next affliction becomes a random minor boon. A Maxroll top pick.

boons.name: Crystal Chalice
boons.note: Major boon: you gain no more minor afflictions. A Maxroll top pick.

boons.name: Sacred Mirror
boons.note: Major boon that duplicates up to 3 Offer rewards. A Maxroll top pick.

boons.name: Holy Water
boons.note: Major boon: using a Fountain grants a minor boon. A Maxroll top pick.

boons.name: Holy Descry
boons.note: Major boon: at 0 Resolve you revive at full Resolve, but lose 50% maximum Resolve and a random boon. Insurance against a run-ending mistake.

boons.name: Priest's Descry
boons.note: Major boon: revives you once at 75% maximum Resolve. Maxroll lists it as a top boon.

boons.name: Imperial Seal
boons.note: Major boon that disables traps, cancelling trap afflictions such as Deadly Snare, Dark Pit and Rapid Quicksand.

boons.name: Silver Descry
boons.note: Major boon: ignore the first Resolve loss from a hit in each room. PoE-Vault singles it out for no-hit challenge runs.

boons.name: Gilded Lyre
boons.note: Minor boon: +100 Inspiration at the start of each floor (per PoEDB). A Maxroll minor pick. Paired with Mellifluous Chorus, a forum player calls it a 'resolve tank'.

boons.name: Rusted Chimes
boons.note: Minor boon and Inspiration source, a Maxroll pick. PoEDB lists it as +30 Inspiration per affliction, the reverse of Maxroll's wording.

boons.name: Mellifluous Chorus
boons.note: 40% less Resolve lost while you have Inspiration. Pairs with Gilded Lyre for a tanky Inspiration setup.

boons.name: Mirror of Fortune
boons.note: Minor boon that duplicates a random Offer reward. A Maxroll pick.

boons.name: Prayer Beads
boons.note: Minor boon: no Resolve loss in the next room. A Maxroll pick.

boons.name: Silver Tongue
boons.note: Minor boon: 50% lower Merchant prices. A Maxroll pick.

boons.name: Bronze Coin + Silver Coin
boons.note: Bronze Coin: picking up Aureus recovers Resolve. Silver Coin: gain 10 Aureus when a hit costs Resolve. PoE-Vault notes that together they give infinite Aureus.

boons.name: Sanguine Vial / Ornate Dagger
boons.note: A forum player suggests them as counters to Spiked Shell or Blunt Sword.

rules.text: Stack Inspiration (cap 1,000). It absorbs Resolve loss before Resolve does, so prioritise it over Resolve. Resolve recovery only helps after you have lost Resolve, which is why the recovery-blocking afflictions are freebies.

Major afflictions only come from Pacts, which you opt into and can read before accepting, so a major affliction can always be skipped. Minor afflictions come from entering rooms with a purple border on the Floor Map.
You cannot hold two copies of the same affliction, so bad afflictions get harder to dodge as your pool fills.
Watch for combos. Ghastly Scythe plus Spiked Exit is run-ending, because Spiked Exit takes Resolve directly. Spiked Exit plus Voodoo Doll is dangerous.

Pacts that sacrifice Maximum Resolve (usually by 25% or 50%, or setting it to 1) are close to free when you have plenty of Inspiration banked. Taking at least one option in a Pact room can also give multiple boons and an Offer.
Once you click an Accursed Pact you must pick one of its options. Notable options: gain 200 Inspiration for losing 200 Resolve, and gain 30 Inspiration at the start of every room.
Indomitable Pact (10 Inspiration at the start of every room) is a trap if you're stacking Inspiration, because your Inspiration resets every room.

Other named Pacts (per PoEDB): Austerity gives 50% lower Merchant prices but monsters drop no Aureus. Apex gives 50% less Resolve lost in Boss Rooms but 100% more elsewhere. Doubling makes Guards Twinned. Dauntless gives 50% more Rare Monsters, each with an extra modifier. Pyrrhic doubles Resolve recovered but cuts max Resolve by 50% of what you recover.
On Floors 1 and 2, take a Pact only if it grants a major boon. A Pact that drains 30 Resolve for a handful of coins is a trap that snowballs into a failed Floor 4.
On Floor 4, if no Divine Orb Offer is visible, take Pacts for their chance at an Offer, even a net-negative one if it isn't too dangerous.

Radiant Fountain (5 Aureus) grants 200 Inspiration and a random boon and removes a random affliction, but each purge rerolls the afflictions on rooms across the Sanctum and can put a run-ending room on your path. Afflicted Fountain (5 Aureus) restores 50% of maximum Resolve but grants a random affliction; avoid it unless you are truly desperate.
You can't get duplicate boons, so each boon you collect raises the odds that your next one is strong. Merchants offer several boons per visit.
The best relics for a Sanctum run grant Inspiration when you receive an affliction (usually 40-50). They roll on large 4x1 or 2x2 relics, and you can stack several.

Melee and low-mobility characters are poorly suited to the Sanctum. Ranged, off-screen-clearing builds with high single-target damage are well suited. A teleport skill is effectively mandatory, and skills that root you in place or have long animation lock are very dangerous.
Glass-cannon builds lose Resolve fast and fail runs. Tanky builds do better because Armour, Evasion and Energy Shield feed Resolve protection. Take defensive boons early on Floors 3 and 4.
The combat afflictions from the Pact of Beidat, Ghorr, K'Tash and Lycia skill gems are not Forbidden Sanctum afflictions. The Unholy Accomplice belt makes Pact skills grant Boons instead.

PoEDB lists newer afflictions that the 3.22 guides do not rate: Corrosive Concoction (major), Shattered Shield, Sharpened Arrowhead, Iron Manacles, Phantom Illusion and Corrupted Lockpick. The defence-related ones mostly hurt builds that rely on Resolve Mitigation, avoidance or Resolve Aegis.

Patches 3.26 to 3.29 did not change afflictions or boons, so the 3.22-era ratings still apply. Patch 3.29 restores flask charges whenever you interact with the Sanctum Map between rooms (except The Writhing Jar) and adds Volatile Vaal Orbs as a Sanctum reward.

remnants.mod: Runic Monsters are Duplicated
remnants.why: Guides rate it the best Remnant reward, and Maxroll's 3.28 strategy ranks it first. It doubles Runic Monsters, which drop logbooks and artifacts. It is a Prefix (mod level 68) from the same pool as the harmful monster mods, not a Suffix.

remnants.mod: 50% increased Quantity of Expedition Logbooks dropped by Runic Monsters
remnants.why: Suffix, mod level 24. One of Maxroll's top-priority Remnants for logbook farming in its 3.28 strategy.

remnants.mod: 40% increased Quantity of Items Dropped by Monsters
remnants.why: Suffix, mod level 1. One of Maxroll's five priority Remnants.

remnants.mod: 50% increased Quantity of Artifacts dropped by Monsters
remnants.why: Suffix, mod level 1. Maxroll lists the monster version as a priority Remnant.

remnants.mod: Runic Monsters have 35% chance to drop an additional Stacked Deck
remnants.why: Suffix, mod level 34. One of Maxroll's five priority Remnants. Opening the decks is a gamble; selling them in bulk is the steadier choice.

remnants.mod: 25% increased Pack size
remnants.why: Suffix. Maxroll calls pack size very valuable in Expedition because it adds Runic Monsters, and more Runic Monsters means more logbooks and Vendor Refresh Currency.

remnants.mod: Monsters are Immune to Physical Damage
remnants.why: Level 1 prefix. Maxroll warns it can completely stop a physical build from killing anything the Remnant affects. Skip it if physical is your main damage type.

remnants.mod: Monsters are Immune to Fire Damage
remnants.why: Level 1 prefix. A build that deals mostly fire damage cannot kill what the Remnant affects. Single-element builds must avoid their own element's immunity.

remnants.mod: Monsters are Immune to Cold Damage
remnants.why: Level 1 prefix. A build that deals mostly cold damage cannot kill what the Remnant affects. Single-element builds must avoid their own element's immunity.

remnants.mod: Monsters are Immune to Lightning Damage
remnants.why: Level 1 prefix. A build that deals mostly lightning damage cannot kill what the Remnant affects. Single-element builds must avoid their own element's immunity.

remnants.mod: Monsters are Immune to Chaos Damage
remnants.why: Level 1 prefix. A build that deals mostly chaos damage cannot kill what the Remnant affects. A 3.29 chaos CoC Occultist guide names it as an Expedition mod it cannot run.

remnants.mod: Monster Hits ignore Physical Damage Reduction
remnants.why: Level 1 prefix. It turns off armour, endurance charges and other physical damage reduction. Forum players say it one-shots armour and block builds. The advice is to skip it on armour builds, especially in Hardcore, or to rely on phys-taken-as-elemental or 'less damage taken' layers.

remnants.mod: Hits against Monsters cannot be Critical Strikes
remnants.why: Prefix, mod level 35 and up. It stops all player crits against Expedition monsters, which breaks crit-scaling and Cast on Critical Strike builds. A 3.29 CoC guide lists it as a mod you just can't run.

remnants.mod: Monsters' Hits are always Critical Strikes
remnants.why: Level 1 prefix. PoE Vault gives 'All Hits Crit' as an example of a downside that can brick a build. It is dangerous without crit-damage reduction or a big life/ES pool.

remnants.mod: Monsters Kill things with 20% or lower Life on Hit
remnants.why: Level 1 prefix that gives monsters a 20% culling strike. It checks life only and ignores energy shield, so it is a one-shot risk for low-life builds and builds that drop low between hits. Read the Remnants and leave this one out of the chain.

remnants.mod: Damage cannot Leech Life from Monsters
remnants.why: Prefix, mod level 35 and up. The same mod line also blocks mana leech, so avoid it if leech is your build's main sustain.

remnants.mod: Monsters' Hits can't be Evaded
remnants.why: Level 1 prefix. It switches off evasion as a defence, so evasion-based builds are hit by every attack.

remnants.mod: Monsters are Immune to Curses
remnants.why: Prefix, mod level 24 and up. Avoid it on curse-reliant builds, such as hexers or curse-on-hit setups that need curse effects for damage or defence.

remnants.mod: Monsters have 100% chance to Avoid being Chilled/Frozen/Ignited/Shocked
remnants.why: Level 1 prefix that makes monsters immune to the four elemental ailments. It hurts ignite-damage, freeze-lock and shock-dependent builds.

remnants.mod: Monsters Penetrate 15% Fire/Cold/Lightning/Chaos Resistance
remnants.why: Level 1 prefixes, one for each resistance. Each cuts your effective resistance against that element by 15%. In the Remnant pool these are the closest thing to a minus-max-res mod. They are dangerous when stacked with damage prefixes.

remnants.mod: Monsters' Hits remove 10% of current Energy Shield / Mana
remnants.why: Prefix, mod level 73 and up. Every hit removes 10% of your current ES or mana. ES/CI builds and mana-reliant builds (MoM, mana-cost spammers) should avoid it.

remnants.mod: Monsters do not grant Flask Charges when Slain
remnants.why: Level 1 prefix that starves flask-reliant builds during the encounter. Avoid it unless you have other ways to generate flask charges.

remnants.mod: Runic Monsters apply Death Geas / 1 random Hex / Petrification on Hit
remnants.why: Prefixes, mod level 46 and up. They debuff you when Runic Monsters hit. Petrification (2 seconds) can lock out melee and face-tank builds.

remnants.mod: Monster hits inflict Freeze (ailment-on-hit prefix)
remnants.why: Prefix, mod level 10. Of the monster ailment-on-hit prefixes (Bleed, Poison, Ignite, Freeze, Shock, Impale), Freeze is the deadliest for builds without freeze immunity.

remnants.mod: Monsters have +5% to all maximum Resistances / +30% to all Resistances
remnants.why: Level 30 prefixes that make monsters tankier. Elemental damage builds lose damage, and the effect grows when other tankiness mods are in the chain.

remnants.mod: Every 4 seconds, Runic Monsters Regenerate 30% of Life over one second
remnants.why: Level 1 prefix. It is bad for slow damage-over-time builds against Runic monsters.

remnants.mod: Monsters have 100% increased Critical Strike Chance against Enemies on Full Life
remnants.why: Prefix related to 'Hits are always Critical Strikes'. It punishes builds without crit damage reduction.

rules.text: Each Remnant has a Prefix that makes unearthed monsters stronger and a Suffix that raises rewards. The good and bad sides always come together, so read both before you include a Remnant.

A Remnant's mods apply to the explosion that detonates it and to every later explosion, never to earlier ones. Plan the whole chain before you detonate, and place risky Remnants late or after the targets you most want buffed.
An Expedition boss gets every Remnant detonated before it is unearthed. Only dig it up late in the chain if your build can handle the stacked prefixes.
Detonation priority: Remnants first, then Runic Monster Markers, then Expedition chests. Take the strong Remnants first and spend the rest of the chain on as many Runic markers as you can.
Skip any immunity Remnant that matches your main damage type. Single-element builds must avoid their own element's immunity.

The Remnant pool has no true '-max resistance' or 'no regeneration' player mod; those are map mods. The closest Remnant equivalents are the 15% resistance penetration prefixes and the monster max-resistance prefixes.

Extreme Archaeology (Atlas keystone): one explosive with 200% increased radius and 100% increased placement range, and monsters spawn with 10% of life missing. Remnant mods then reach almost every unearthed monster, so you cannot avoid bad prefixes.
Ancient Writings (Atlas): +2 Remnants per Expedition and a 30% chance for each Remnant to have an extra Suffix, giving more options to pick from.
Buried Knowledge (Atlas): 50% increased Quantity of Logbooks from Runic Monsters and 20% more Runic Monster Markers.

Distinguished Demolitionist (35% radius, 20% more explosives) and Explosive Placement Distance (20% range) let the chain reach every important Remnant with explosives left over for Runic markers. The explosive-count part does nothing under Extreme Archaeology.

Atlas notables can make detonation chains travel 25% faster or 25% slower. Since 3.28 the small nodes on the path to Ancient Decay give 25% slower detonation, and two new small nodes give 25% faster detonation. Ancient Decay itself makes monsters spawn with an extra 20% of life missing.
Expedition Scarab of Archaeology (limit 1) adds 2 Prefixes and 2 Suffixes to every Remnant. It is very powerful but sharply raises build requirements, because the extra prefixes add more danger.

Expedition Scarab of Runefinding (limit 2): 100% more Runic Monster Markers, which roughly triples artifact and Vendor Refresh Currency drops. Verisium Powder (limit 1): 50% more explosives and 80% increased radius. Maxroll's 3.28 strategy runs 2x Runefinding plus Verisium Powder.

Expedition Scarab of Infusion (new in 3.28, limit 1): logbooks dropped in the area always have 4 implicits, and monsters gain difficulty and reward for each Remnant you detonate, so every extra Remnant raises both danger and loot.
Pick open map layouts such as Dunes and Jungle Valley. Cemetery is open, but the Expedition can spawn in poor spots with less access to the best Remnants.

Controls: the chain starts at the detonator next to the NPC. Shift+V undoes the last placement, explosives fire in the order placed, and each must be within maximum range of the previous one. Any marker inside an explosive's radius gets dug up.
In Logbooks, side areas glow green when an explosive's radius covers them; each holds 2-6 reward chests. Runic monsters inside Logbooks cannot drop Logbooks.
Since 3.28, when many Remnant mods are active, the list of mods affecting excavated monsters and chests splits into multiple columns.
3.29: Expedition got no major changes and the Remnant mechanics still apply. Tujen can no longer trade for Catalysts, and since 3.28 he no longer sells Cluster or Abyss Jewels.

goals.name: sell
tips: PoE Vault: only S-tier rooms reliably sell. The temples that sell contain Doryani's Institute, Locus of Corruption or Apex of Ascension.
Maxroll: most Incursion profit comes from selling temples. Selling a Locus temple is always right unless you want to gamble, and Doryani's temples should usually be sold too.
Price a temple by its most valuable connected room (Maxroll).

Once all 12 incursions are done, ask Alva to itemize the temple into a Chronicle of Atzoatl instead of opening portals. It opens in a personal Map Device, gives six portals, and you can right-click it to view the layout.
Incursion Scarab of Timelines: the final Architect killed in the map drops an itemized temple. It copies the current layout with rerolled room tiers, so you get extra temples to sell.
Old price snapshot from the forum, before 3.29: Locus temple about 1.7 divine, Doryani temple about 60 chaos. Check current prices before you trust these.

goals.name: corrupt-items
tips: Altar of Corruption: corrupts one uncorrupted weapon, armour piece, jewellery piece, quiver or jewel. The four outcomes are equally likely: two corruption implicits replacing the existing ones, a socket-colour change, a reroll into an influenced rare of the same base, or the item is destroyed. Flasks cannot be used.

3.29: the outcome that turned all sockets white was removed. Sockets are now white by default, and the outcome turns every white socket non-white, ignoring attribute colour weights. On a socketless item it does nothing.
A non-unique Sacrificial Garb that gets the two-implicit outcome turns into Shadowstitch.
The influenced-rare outcome respects metamods. Hinekora's Lock cannot preview the altar result (since 3.23).
Paquate's chain lowers player maximum resistances across the whole temple: -6% at T1, -8% at T2, -10% at T3.
Never kill Paquate while you still want a Locus in this temple: a killed architect cannot appear again.

goals.name: corrupt-gems
tips: The Lapidary Lens works like two Vaal Orbs on one skill, transfigured or support gem. It is the only non-div-card way to get two of: level 21 (+1 above max for Exceptional or Awakened supports), 21-23% quality, Vaal version.
Odds on a 20/20 gem with no Vaal version (wiki maths): 3.17% for 21/23, 21.0% for level 21 with quality of 20% or more, 25% for level 21 at any quality.
How it rolls: the first outcome is 1/4 each for no change, Vaal version, level +/-1, or quality change. The second is 1/3 from the remaining options. The result can be no change at all.
The only real bricks are lost quality or an unwanted Vaal/non-Vaal switch, because a -1 level can be levelled back.
Never kill Zalatl while you still want Doryani's Institute in this temple.

goals.name: upgrade-uniques
tips: The Altar of Sacrifice swaps a unique equipment item for a random unique of the same item class, or upgrades a temple unique when you add its matching Vial.

Vial upgrades: Apep's Slumber + Vial of Awakening -> Apep's Supremacy; Tempered Flesh/Spirit/Mind + Vial of Transcendence -> the Transcendent version; Sacrificial Heart + Vial of Sacrifice -> Zerphi's Heart; Soul Catcher + Vial of the Ghost -> Soul Ripper.
The altar works once per temple. Since 3.20 it cannot be used on unique jewels, flasks or maps.
The Corruption Chamber line raises the Omnitect's chance to drop a Vial of Sacrifice.

goals.name: run-yourself
tips: Maxroll: Atlas of Worlds and Wealth of the Vaal temples are worth running yourself when no better room is present.
Factory gives 60% increased item quantity across the temple, but monsters get 60% more life and the Omnitect 35% more life.
While the temple has an Atlas of Worlds room, Temple Architects drop additional Scarabs (since 3.28.0).
The Vaal Omnitect drops rares with Incursion mods themed on the temple's rooms, and has a higher chance to drop those rooms' Vials. Higher-tier rooms mean more rares.
Sources disagree on the Omnitect: Maxroll says it is only worth running alongside another room of interest, while PoE Vault calls the boss room huge for loot.

goals.name: upgrade-neighbours
tips: Shrine of Empowerment (T1) upgrades one random adjacent, connected room by a tier. Sanctum of Unity (T2) upgrades two.
Temple Nexus (T3) upgrades every adjacent room by a tier, connected or not. Put it next to the room you want pushed up.
At T3 monsters get 20% attack and cast speed. Monster drops are +1 item level, but area level and chest items are unchanged.

goals.name: open-paths
tips: Clearing an Incursion drops one guaranteed Stone of Passage if at least one door in that room is still closed. Stones vanish when you leave the Incursion, so plan connections to your valuable rooms.
Explosives-chain rooms hold Flashpowder Kegs. Each one opens a passage you did not unlock during the incursions, or a Sealed Coffer (1/2/3 by tier).
You reach the Apex of Atzoatl with Stones of Passage during incursions, or with Flashpowder Kegs during the present-day run.

rules.text: A temple takes exactly 12 incursions. After that, Alva stops appearing in maps, and when only one or two remain she offers just that many. The temple has 13 room slots: the 12 you shape plus the fixed Apex of Atzoatl, which holds the Vaal Omnitect.

Maps normally give 3 incursions, so a temple takes 4 maps. The Atlas notable Artefacts of the Vaal makes incursion maps always have 4, so a temple takes 3 maps. Do 4 of the incursions on tier 16 maps to keep the temple at area level 83.

Each incursion has two architects. Kill the non-resident (invading) architect to upgrade the room to the resident's next tier, up to T3. Kill the resident to change the room to the survivor's T1 room. Kill neither and nothing changes. In-game, the resident stands in the bottom-left half of the room.
Maxroll's shorthand: slay the top architect to upgrade the room and the bottom one to switch it. Kill the architect first, then clear the Incursion for Stones of Passage.
Untiered (T0) rooms such as Antechamber or Banquet Hall have no resident. Killing either of the two random architects turns the room into the survivor's T1 room.
An architect you kill cannot appear again for the rest of that temple. Never kill Paquate (Locus) or Zalatl (Doryani's) while you still want their room.

A room that reaches T3 is never offered again, and its architect stops appearing as a room owner. The Entrance (fixed at the bottom) and the Apex (fixed at the top) can never be picked as incursion rooms either.

Layout rules: the temple starts with untiered and T1 rooms in 11 connectable spaces. A room family appears only once per temple (one Corruption Chamber rules out a Catalyst), and no two rooms share a resident architect.

Wiki strategy for a T3 Locus or Doryani's: (1) with no wanted room present, change rooms until one appears; (2) once it is present, push other rooms to T3 so they stop being offered; (3) if the wanted room still needs upgrades after an incursion, don't talk to Alva again in that map, because the same room can't be offered twice in one area.

Resource Reallocation (Atlas notable): killing a non-resident architect has a 40% chance to add an extra upgrade tier, which can jump a room from T1 straight to T3. Each small Incursion Upgrade Chance node gives 10%.

Contested Development (Atlas notable): killing the resident architect carries the room's tier over to the survivor's room instead of resetting it to T1. For example, an unwanted T2 room can become a T2 Catalyst of Corruption.
Clearing an Incursion drops one Stone of Passage only while at least one door in that room is still closed. Stones vanish when you leave the Incursion.

Incursion Scarab of Timelines (limit 1): the final Architect killed in the map drops an itemized temple. It copies the current layout with rerolled room tiers, and players use it to dupe temples whose layout has a corruption room.

Forum strategy (Oct 2024, edited Feb 2025, pre-3.29): Timelines is mandatory whenever a corruption room of any tier is on the layout and reachable. It is optional when that room is unreachable, and on average not a net gain with only Gemcutter rooms. Once a corruption-room upgrade appears, finish the map without opening the Incursion to keep the Timelines duplication chance.

Other Incursion scarabs: Incursion Scarab (map contains Alva, limit 1); Scarab of Invasion (12-16 extra Incursion packs, limit 3); Scarab of Champions (35% chance all monsters are at least Magic, 15% increased pack size, limit 2).

Once the temple is complete, Alva can itemize it into a tradeable Chronicle of Atzoatl instead of opening portals. It opens 'The Temple of Atzoatl' in a personal Map Device with six portals. Right-click it to view the layout.

The Apex of Atzoatl is a fixed, untiered boss room at the top of the temple and cannot be built. You reach it with Stones of Passage during incursions or with Flashpowder Kegs from an Explosives-chain room during the present-day run.
Data note: Ahuana owns the Sacrificial Chamber -> Hall of Offerings -> Apex of Ascension chain. The Sparring Room -> Arena of Valour -> Hall of Champions chain belongs to Ticaba.
Prices in the sources are old (Maxroll guide Aug 2023; forum snapshot from before 3.29). Use them only to rank rooms, and check live prices before selling.
